\chapter{Disaster and Warnings}
\label{ch:ml-disaster-and-warnings}
\hlchaptermodality{374}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say a warning, a disaster, a rescue operation, a state of emergency and to evacuate.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 374: I can say a warning, a disaster, a rescue operation, a state of emergency and to evacuate.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{മുന്നറിയിപ്പ്} (munnaṟiyippŭ)}{മുന്നറിയിപ്പ് (munnaṟiyippŭ)}]{\ml{മുന്നറിയിപ്പ്} (munnaṟiyippŭ) — a warning}

\label{lesson:ML-C374-munnariyippu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to loot, then the Malayalam for to smash.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{മുന്നറിയിപ്പ്}}
\textbf{\ml{മുന്നറിയിപ്പ്}} — \emph{munnaṟiyippŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}a warning\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ശക്തമായ} \ml{മഴയെക്കുറിച്ച്} \ml{സർക്കാർ} \ml{മുന്നറിയിപ്പ്} \ml{നൽകി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{śaktamāya maḻayekkuṟiccŭ sarkkār munnaṟiyippŭ nalki.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The government gave a warning about heavy rain.
\end{quote}

\ml{മുൻ}, before, + \ml{അറിയിപ്പ്}, a notice: news given in advance.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{മുന്നറിയിപ്പ്}} (\emph{munnaṟiyippŭ}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{മുൻ} (\emph{mun}), \textquotedblleft{}before, in front\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 5020), and \ml{അറിയിപ്പ്} (\emph{aṟiyippŭ}), \textquotedblleft{}a notice\textquotedblright{}, from \ml{അറിയുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to know\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 314): letting people know before it happens.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{munnaṟiyippŭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{munnaṟiyippŭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śaktamāya maḻayekkuṟiccŭ sarkkār munnaṟiyippŭ nalki.} — The government gave a warning about heavy rain.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to loot, then the Malayalam for to smash, then say \emph{munnaṟiyippŭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{മുന്നറിയിപ്പ്} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A warning\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ദുരന്തം} (durantaṁ)}{ദുരന്തം (durantaṁ)}]{\ml{ദുരന്തം} (durantaṁ) — a disaster; a tragedy}

\label{lesson:ML-C374-durantam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to smash, then the Malayalam for a warning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ദുരന്തം}}
\textbf{\ml{ദുരന്തം}} — \emph{durantaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}a disaster; a tragedy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ആ} \ml{ദുരന്തത്തിൽ} \ml{ഒരുപാട്} \ml{വീടുകൾ} \ml{തകർന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā durantattil orupāṭŭ vīṭukaḷ takarnnu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Many houses collapsed in that disaster.
\end{quote}

Also the tragic end of a story.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ദുരന്തം}} (\emph{durantaṁ}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{duranta}, \textquotedblleft{}having a bad end; miserable\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), made of \emph{dur-}, \textquotedblleft{}bad\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{anta}, \textquotedblleft{}end\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{durantaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{durantaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā durantattil orupāṭŭ vīṭukaḷ takarnnu.} — Many houses collapsed in that disaster.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to smash, then the Malayalam for a warning, then say \emph{durantaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ദുരന്തം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A disaster; a tragedy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{രക്ഷാപ്രവർത്തനം} (rakṣāpravarttanaṁ)}{രക്ഷാപ്രവർത്തനം (rakṣāpravarttanaṁ)}]{\ml{രക്ഷാപ്രവർത്തനം} (rakṣāpravarttanaṁ) — a rescue operation}

\label{lesson:ML-C374-raksapravarttanam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a warning, then the Malayalam for a disaster.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{രക്ഷാപ്രവർത്തനം}}
\textbf{\ml{രക്ഷാപ്രവർത്തനം}} — \emph{rakṣāpravarttanaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}a rescue operation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{രാത്രി} \ml{മുഴുവൻ} \ml{രക്ഷാപ്രവർത്തനം} \ml{നടന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rātri muḻuvan rakṣāpravarttanaṁ naṭannu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The rescue operation went on all night.
\end{quote}

\ml{രക്ഷ}, protection, + \ml{പ്രവർത്തനം}, work, activity.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{രക്ഷാപ്രവർത്തനം}} (\emph{rakṣāpravarttanaṁ}) is built from two Sanskrit words: \emph{rakṣā}, \textquotedblleft{}protection, care\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10551), and \emph{pravartana}, \textquotedblleft{}moving forward, setting in motion\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rakṣāpravarttanaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rakṣāpravarttanaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rātri muḻuvan rakṣāpravarttanaṁ naṭannu.} — The rescue operation went on all night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a warning, then the Malayalam for a disaster, then say \emph{rakṣāpravarttanaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{രക്ഷാപ്രവർത്തനം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A rescue operation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{അടിയന്തരാവസ്ഥ} (aṭiyantarāvastha)}{അടിയന്തരാവസ്ഥ (aṭiyantarāvastha)}]{\ml{അടിയന്തരാവസ്ഥ} (aṭiyantarāvastha) — a state of emergency}

\label{lesson:ML-C374-atiyantaravastha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a disaster, then the Malayalam for a rescue operation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{അടിയന്തരാവസ്ഥ}}
\textbf{\ml{അടിയന്തരാവസ്ഥ}} — \emph{aṭiyantarāvastha} — \textquotedblleft{}a state of emergency\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{വെള്ളപ്പൊക്കം} \ml{കാരണം} \ml{ജില്ലയിൽ} \ml{അടിയന്തരാവസ്ഥ} \ml{പ്രഖ്യാപിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{veḷḷappokkaṁ kāraṇaṁ jillayil aṭiyantarāvastha prakhyāpiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Because of the flood a state of emergency was declared in the district.
\end{quote}

\ml{അടിയന്തര}, urgent, + \ml{അവസ്ഥ}, a state: a new noun, not the adjective.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{അടിയന്തരാവസ്ഥ}} (\emph{aṭiyantarāvastha}) joins \ml{അടിയന്തര} (\emph{aṭiyantara}), \textquotedblleft{}urgent\textquotedblright{}, and Sanskrit \emph{avasthā}, \textquotedblleft{}a state, a condition\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 872), borrowed whole: the condition of a place when everything is urgent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṭiyantarāvastha}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṭiyantarāvastha}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{veḷḷappokkaṁ kāraṇaṁ jillayil aṭiyantarāvastha prakhyāpiccu.} — Because of the flood a state of emergency was declared in the district.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a disaster, then the Malayalam for a rescue operation, then say \emph{aṭiyantarāvastha} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{അടിയന്തരാവസ്ഥ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A state of emergency\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഒഴിപ്പിക്കുക} (oḻippikkuka)}{ഒഴിപ്പിക്കുക (oḻippikkuka)}]{\ml{ഒഴിപ്പിക്കുക} (oḻippikkuka) — to evacuate}

\label{lesson:ML-C374-olippikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a rescue operation, then the Malayalam for a state of emergency.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഒഴിപ്പിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ഒഴിപ്പിക്കുക}} — \emph{oḻippikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to evacuate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പോലീസ്} \ml{ഗ്രാമത്തിലെ} \ml{ആളുകളെ} \ml{ഒഴിപ്പിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pōlīsŭ grāmattile āḷukaḷe oḻippiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police evacuated the people of the village.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ഒഴിപ്പിച്ചു}, \emph{oḻippiccu}.

To make a place empty of people, before a flood or a fire.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഒഴിപ്പിക്കുക}} (\emph{oḻippikkuka}) is native Dravidian, the causative of \ml{ഒഴിയുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to leave off, to be free from, to be empty\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1009).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oḻippikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oḻippikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pōlīsŭ grāmattile āḷukaḷe oḻippiccu.} — The police evacuated the people of the village.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a rescue operation, then the Malayalam for a state of emergency, then say \emph{oḻippikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
